players.product: commercial & industrial electrical contracting for data centers

quarterly_data.signal: MYR Group 10-K: 2025 contract revenues were $3,657,889 thousand (2024: $3,362,290 thousand) - T&D $2,002,440 thousand (54.7% of revenue, +6.5% year over year) and C&I $1,655,449 thousand (45.3%, +11.7%). Gross margin was 11.6% (2024: 8.6%); operating income was $157,610 thousand in T&D (7.9% margin vs 3.7%) and $97,207 thousand in C&I (5.9% vs 3.2%); net income $118,416 thousand (2024: $30,263 thousand), diluted EPS $7.53, EBITDA $232,721 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue $3,657,889 thousand; T&D $2,002,440 thousand; C&I $1,655,449 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: MYR Group 10-K: 2025 revenue by market - transmission $1,198,584 thousand (32.8%), distribution $803,856 thousand (22.0%), C&I electrical construction $1,655,449 thousand (45.2%); fixed-price contracts made up 84.5% of C&I revenue and 34.3% of T&D revenue.

MYR Group 10-K: backlog at December 31, 2025 was $2,824,268 thousand (December 31, 2024: $2,576,418 thousand) - T&D $1,018,116 thousand, C&I $1,806,152 thousand - of which $2,437,765 thousand is estimated to be recognized within 12 months; it included a proportionate share of unconsolidated joint venture backlog of $176.1 million. Remaining performance obligations were $2.52 billion, with approximately 85% expected to be recognized within twelve months and approximately 95% or more within twenty-four months.

MYR Group 10-K: capital expenditures were approximately $94.4 million in 2025 (2024: $75.9 million), most of them supporting T&D opportunities; operating activities provided $326.6 million of cash (2024: $87.1 million); MYR Group had approximately $33.9 million of outstanding purchase obligations for construction equipment to be paid in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex $94.4 million; $33.9 million equipment purchase obligations

quarterly_data.signal: MYR Group 10-K (management outlook): 'Our C&I bidding opportunities remain strong and we believe we will see continued opportunities in the primary markets we serve such as data centers, transportation, health care, manufacturing, clean energy and warehousing'; the company expects the need for expanding public infrastructure in the U.S. and Canada to offer C&I opportunity for several years and long-term C&I growth to generally track the overall growth of the regions it serves.
